(Summit, Mississippi) | college = * [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]] (2020–2024) * [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 39 | draft_team = [[Toronto Raptors]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team2 = →[[Raptors 905]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League Third Team]] ([[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]) * [[NBA G League]] All Defensive Team (2026) * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025]]) * First-team All-[[Conference USA|C-USA]] (2023) * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2024) * Third-team All-C-USA (2022) * [[Conference USA men's basketball tournament|C-USA tournament]] MVP ([[2023 Conference USA men's basketball tournament|2023]]) *NCAA Men's Final Four All-Tournament Team (2023) }} '''Alijah Randall Edwin Martin''' (born December 26, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic Owls]] and the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==High school career== Martin attended [[North Pike School District|North Pike High School]] in [[Summit, Mississippi]].{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2024 |title=Alijah Martin: College Basketball Player, University of Florida |url=https://www.theballersmagazine.com/post/alijah-martin-college-basketball-player-university-of-florida-full-interview |access-date=April 8, 2025 |website=The Ballers Magazine |language=en}} A multi-sport athlete, he played [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]], passing for 2,100 yards and rushing for 1,300 yards in his senior season.{{Cite web |last=Brockway |first=Kevin |title=Grad transfer guard Alijah Martin explains why he left FAU for Florida basketball |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/09/26/florida-basketball-guard-alijah-martin-on-why-he-left-fau-for-uf/75304552007/ |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}} In his senior basketball season, he averaged 25.4 points, 8.7 rebounds, and 3.4 steals per game, before committing to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]].{{Cite web |title=North Pike’s Alijah Martin verbally commits to FAU |url=https://www.wjtv.com/sports/friday-night-rewind/north-pikes-alijah-martin-verbally-commits-to-fau/ |website=WJTV}} ==College career== After playing sparingly as a freshman for the Owls, he averaged 13.9 points and 5.3 rebounds per game as a sophomore, being named to the all-conference third team.{{Cite web |last=Wallace |first=Eric J. |title=5 things to know about Florida Atlantic basketball star sophomore Alijah Martin |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/2023/03/21/alijah-martin-5-things-about-florida-atlantic-basketball-star-march-madness-fau/70034019007/ |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=The Palm Beach Post |archive-date=March 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322180046/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/2023/03/21/alijah-martin-5-things-about-florida-atlantic-basketball-star-march-madness-fau/70034019007/ |language=en-US}} The following season, he averaged 13.4 points and 5.3 rebounds per game, helping lead Florida Atlantic to the school's first ever Final Four appearance.{{Cite web |last=Weinberger |first=Zach |title=Johnell Davis joins Alijah Martin: Declare for 2023 NBA Draft but preserve college eligibility |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2023/04/09/faus-alijah-martin-declares-for-nba-draft-but-could-still-return-to-owls/70097765007/ |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=The Palm Beach Post |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410040057/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2023/04/09/faus-alijah-martin-declares-for-nba-draft-but-could-still-return-to-owls/70097765007/?utm_campaign=snd-autopilot&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter_pbpsports |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=April 10, 2023 |title=Alijah Martin declares for NBA Draft, but it may not be end of his college career |url=https://www.wptv.com/sports/college-sports/florida-atlantic-university/alijah-martin-declares-for-nba-draft-but-it-may-not-be-end-of-his-college-career |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=WPTV News Channel 5 West Palm |language=en}} In his final season with the Owls, he averaged 13.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game, before entering the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{Cite web |last=Pugliese |first=Nick |title=Alijah Martin joins exodus of Florida Atlantic basketball players entering transfer portal |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/04/06/alijah-martin-joins-exodus-of-florida-atlantic-owls-entering-transfer-portal/73230768007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409150527/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/04/06/alijah-martin-joins-exodus-of-florida-atlantic-owls-entering-transfer-portal/73230768007/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 9, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}} In April 2024, Martin announced his decision to transfer to the [[University of Florida]].{{Cite web |date=April 21, 2024 |title=Final Four star Martin going from FAU to Florida |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39987927/alijah-martin-part-fau-final-four-run-joining-florida |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=April 22, 2024 |title=Former FAU standout Alijah Martin signs with Florida over Alabama, Arkansas, Michigan and others |url=https://apnews.com/article/alijah-martin-florida-fau-a196e04b87c4abdc871b21321eba5eda |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}} He made an instant impact, emerging as the Gators' starting shooting guard.{{Cite web |last=Brockway |first=Kevin |title=How Alijah Martin's NCAA Tournament experience could help Florida basketball in March Madness |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2025/03/20/florida-basketball-guard-alijah-martin-adds-postseason-pedigree-to-uf-roster/82543588007/ |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}} In a game against [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]], he recorded 32 points, nine rebounds, and five assists, leading Florida to a 93–68 victory.{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2024 |title=FAU transfer Alijah Martin sees Final Four potential in unbeaten Gators |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2024/11/22/florida-gators-basketball-fau-transfer-alijah-martin-todd-golden/ |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}} Against [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]], he scored 17 points in a 79–73 victory.{{Cite web |title=Florida's Martin gets second chance at a championship |url=https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/sports/2025/04/07/florida-gators--houston-cougars--final-four--college-basketball--alijah-martin |access-date=April 8, 2025 |website=baynews9.com |language=en}} In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship Game]] against [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], he tallied seven points, helping lead the Gators to the school's third national championship.{{Cite news |last=Schnell |first=Lindsay |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Florida’s Alijah Martin will talk about his second chance at the Final Four forever |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6263464/2025/04/08/florida-basketball-alijah-martin-fau-ncaa-title/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} ==Professional career== On June 25, 2025, Martin was selected with the 39th overall pick by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]].RotoWire Staff. "Raptors’ Alijah Martin: Selected by Raptors." *CBS Sports*, June 26, 2025. [https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-alijah-martin-selected-by-raptors/ cbssports.com]. Retrieved June 26, 2025. On July 10, the Raptors announced that they had signed Martin to a [[two-way contract]]. He made 23 appearances for Toronto during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 2.2 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Alijah Martin 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702656/alijah-martin|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 2, 2026, Martin re-signed with the Raptors on a two-year, $4.76 million contract.{{Cite web |date=July 2, 2026 |title=RAPTORS SIGN MARTIN |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-martin |access-date=July 4, 2026 |website=raptors.com |language=en}}
